title: Ellington wants him; loyalty to Chick Webb
summary: Ellington's band tries to hire him, but he stays with Webb out of loyalty despite lower pay.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So you were saying -- I'm sorry I interrupted you. You were saying, talking about Duke Ellington coming back.

So they come along, Duke Ellington, you know, want me to go in his band. Chief was the first trumpet player, you know. Something happened to him. And they're looking for fresh trumpet player (inaudible) the guy left Chick. They listen to me play. They want somebody like me. (Inaudible) I didn't want (inaudible) Chick, I get along in love with the guy. I love his music and the things that he done for me and everything else, you know. So I don't want to leave.

I came here, you know, with Duke Ellington, and I had respect for that music, but I feel as if I have to develop myself. I feel better in Chick's band than I do in Duke's band. Then I knew more about jazz then, and I know exactly where I fit the best, and I don't think I would fit in Duke's band as much as I did in his band.

So I -- so they drop out of this thing, different guys like -- (inaudible) Duke can pay. You ain't never going to make money with Chick, man, all this. I say, I know that, but, you know, this guy give me my first break, you know what I mean. I don't want to leave because that be happen to him too often. Every time he get somebody that's getting into the spotlight, they attract him, Fletcher Henderson or Duke, often
be money less. So how do you want to live? All right.
